_summary: Read: the loss is plainly visible at 300 m on three of five poses. Several lod1 meshes drop facade detail that reads at chase-camera distance: De Bijenkorf loses its lettering, mullions and gable curve; Hotel de l'Europe next to the Munttoren loses its banding and ornament; the Stopera/stadhuis and its neighbours lose every window. Westerkerk and Munttoren-Amstel lose only a few dozen px. Savings are 4-12 % of drawn triangles (80k-227k per frame). On these frames the rule is not a no-visible-loss cut; it needs better lod1s or a per-model exemption first.
westerkerk-prinsengracht/far300: Near-invisible: 1,729 px beyond noise, a few small rooftop pieces in the distance. The six extra swaps between 300 and 450 m were behind the camera, so the frame is identical to the 450 m one.
westerkerk-prinsengracht/far450: Identical frame to 300 m at this pose (same triangles, same pixels); the Westerkerk itself is 720 m from the eye and was already the same in both.
munttoren-amstel/far300: Small loss: one brick block's windows go from glazed slots to darker flat panels. 6,521 px. You would not notice it riding.
zuiderkerk-zwanenburgwal/far300: Clearly visible: the large cream building (stadhuis / Stopera, 372 m) loses every window and becomes a blank slab; the foreground roofs lose their window rows. 97,109 px.
damrak-centraal/far300: Clearly visible: De Bijenkorf (303 m, just over the threshold) loses its lettering, window mullions and the curved gable; the windows become dark blobs. Large noise floor here is animation elsewhere in the frame; the crop follows only changes beyond it.
rokin-dam/far300: Clearly visible: Hotel de l'Europe (327 m) loses its striped brick and ornament, and the brick row behind the Munttoren loses its window frames. Worst pair of the five.
